title: Cheese and Herb Börek Spiral
summary: A golden, crisp filo spiral filled with a herby mix of feta, Monterey Jack and goat cheese, baked until deeply golden and cut into wedges.
equipment: 25 cm round tin or ovenproof frying pan

ingredients.item: Monterey Jack or other mild melting cheese, grated
mixed soft herbs (dill, parsley, mint, coriander), chopped
large sheets filo pastry (about 33 x 46 cm), thawed

steps.title: Filling
steps.text: Mix the 225 g feta, 115 g Monterey Jack, 70 g goat cheese, 60 g herbs, spring onions, 2 eggs and ¼ tsp pepper, then chill covered.

steps.title: Butter
steps.text: Oven 190°C, melt the 140 g butter in a small pan, swirling, until the foaming stops but the solids are not browned, 5-7 min.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Lay 1 sheet of filo with the long side toward you, brush with butter, top with a second sheet and brush again.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Spoon one-third of the filling along the near edge, roll up into a loose rope, then gently scrunch it shorter like a concertina.

steps.title: Coil
steps.text: Coil the rope in the middle of the lined tin, then repeat twice more, joining each rope to the end of the spiral.

steps.title: Patch
steps.text: Use the remaining 3 sheets of filo, buttered and scrunched, to patch any gaps or wrap the outer edge.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush the top generously with butter and scatter over the sesame and nigella seeds.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake until deep golden and crisp, 35-40 min, then cool on a rack for 10 min before cutting into wedges.

tips: Keep the filo covered with a damp cloth as you work so it doesn't dry out and crack.
Scrunch the filled rope gently like a concertina so it coils without splitting.
Use the last few sheets of filo to patch any gaps so the filling doesn't leak out during baking.
storage: Best served the day it's baked while the pastry is crisp; keep any leftovers covered in the fridge and reheat in the oven until hot (71°C) in the centre. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
